skill.name: cohere-v2-python
skill.description: Guides users through Cohere v2 Python chat, JSON Schema mode, entity extraction, classification, validation, and production integration patterns.
skill.summary: Build Cohere v2 Python entity extraction with validated structured outputs.
skill.author: ActiveInferenceInstitute

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, placeholder API-key examples, and reference URLs. No prompt-injection text or malicious exfiltration behavior was found, but one insecure database credential example should be corrected.

remediation.suggestion: Replace root/root database credentials with environment variables or placeholders. Recommend a least-privileged database account for stored extraction results.

remediation.issue: API key examples can be safer
remediation.suggestion: Show CO_API_KEY environment variable setup as the primary option. Avoid inline API key placeholders except when clearly marked as non-production.

semantic_findings.title: Insecure Database Credential Example
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md shows a SurrealDB storage example using root/root credentials while persisting extracted entities. Users may copy this pattern into real workflows and expose writable data stores.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example directly hardcodes root/root credentials and opens a database connection. It is not malicious, but it encourages an unsafe default credential pattern.

content.value_statement: Teams need reliable structured data from unstructured text. This skill shows how to use Cohere v2 Python and JSON Schema mode for validated extraction.
actual_capabilities: Initialize Cohere ClientV2 and send basic chat requests.
Define JSON Schema response formats for validated model outputs.
Extract single entities, entity arrays, resumes, invoices, and structured records.
Use enums, nested objects, references, formats, and required fields in schemas.
Design batch extraction workflows with parsing and storage patterns.
Troubleshoot schema limits, latency, token usage, and API error handling.
limitations: Requires a Cohere API key and network access to Cohere services.
Examples are documentation patterns, not a packaged runtime or SDK wrapper.
JSON Schema mode does not support every JSON Schema constraint.
Users must handle privacy, consent, and retention for sensitive source text.

use_cases.title: Create Document Extraction Pipelines
use_cases.description: Extract validated fields from documents for databases, search indexes, and internal systems.

use_cases.title: Add Structured AI Features
use_cases.description: Build product workflows that classify text and return predictable fields for application logic.

use_cases.title: Analyze Research Corpora
use_cases.description: Identify people, organizations, locations, dates, and events across large text collections.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Chat Request
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a first Cohere v2 request.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to show a minimal Cohere v2 Python chat request. Include setup, model selection, and response handling.

prompt_templates.title: Single Entity Schema
prompt_templates.scenario: Design a small extraction task with required fields.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a JSON Schema mode request that extracts one organization, person, date, and location from text.

prompt_templates.title: Batch Document Extraction
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan a Python pipeline that extracts entities from many documents, validates results, and logs failures.

prompt_templates.title: Production Extraction Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Review an advanced implementation before launch.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my Cohere v2 extraction design for schema quality, error handling, privacy, latency, and cost controls.

output_examples.input: Extract contact details from a business card.
output_examples.output: A schema plan with required contact fields, optional company details, and validation notes for email and phone values.

output_examples.input: Classify customer feedback by sentiment and product aspect.
output_examples.output: A constrained classification design with allowed sentiment values and clear aspect-level extraction guidance.

output_examples.input: Review an entity extraction workflow for production readiness.
output_examples.output: A checklist covering schema design, retries, privacy handling, token monitoring, and downstream validation.

best_practices: Use environment variables or secret managers for Cohere API keys.
Keep schemas small at first, then add optional fields after validation succeeds.
Redact sensitive text before sending documents to external model APIs.
anti_patterns: Hardcoding API keys, database passwords, or production endpoints in examples or applications.
Relying on free-form JSON mode when a strict schema is required.
Sending medical, financial, or personal data without approval and retention controls.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps build Cohere v2 Python workflows that return validated structured data from text.

faq.question: Does it include runnable application code?
faq.answer: No. It provides documentation, examples, and implementation guidance for your own Python code.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Do I need a Cohere API key?
faq.answer: Yes. Cohere API calls require a valid key and access to Cohere services.

faq.question: Can it enforce exact output structures?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains JSON Schema mode for required fields, enums, nested objects, and formats.

faq.question: Can I use it with sensitive documents?
faq.answer: Yes, but you must apply privacy review, redaction, consent, and retention controls first.
